To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
S100B protects against the pro-apototic effects of ethanol and that these effects may be linked to PI-3K and NF-kappaB activation.
S100B prevents ethanol-associated apoptosis of rhombencephalon neurons and this effect is linked to PI-3K activation and the up-regulated expression of NF-kappaB pro-survival target genes.

S100B is a neuroprotective agent that can reduce ethanol-associated apoptosis of rhombencephalon neurons in vitro, and that this neuroprotective effect is mediated through activation of PI-3K and its downstream targets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel neuroprotective mechanisms against ethanol-associated apoptosis of rhombencephalon neurons.
the neuroprotective properties of S100B in ethanol-treated fetal rhombencepahlic cultures.
the neuroprotective actions of S100B in the developing brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
S100B's anti-apoptotic actions are associated with activation of the PI3K-->pAKT-->XIAP and PI3K-->Bcl-2-->pAkt-->XIAP pathways, but not with the MAPKK-->p42/p4 MAPK pathway.

S100B is a neurotrophic factor which can protect fetal rhombencepahlic neurons from the pro-apoptosis effects of ethanol by up-regulating the PI-3k-->pAkt-->NF-kappaB-->XIAP-->Bcl-2 pro-survival pathways.
S100B protects ethanol-treated fetal rhombencepahlic neurons from apoptosis via activation of the PI3K-->p-Akt-->NF-kappaB pro-survival signaling pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
S100B is an important neuroprotective protein released by astrocytes following activation of 5-HT1A receptors.
S100B can prevent apoptosis in ethanol-exposed fetal rhombencepahlic neurons by activating the PI-3 kinase pathway.
S100B can prevent the pro-apoptosis effects of ethanol on developing fetal rhombencepahlic neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that

S100B is a potent anti-apoptotic factor for fetal rhombencepahlic neurons and that the neuroprotective actions of S100B appear to be associated with PI-3K activation and up-regulation of XIAP and BCL-2.
S100B has a pro-survival effect on fetal rhombencphalic neurons that are exposed to ethanol.
S100B has the potential to be a novel therapeutic target to reduce ethanol-associated apoptosis and the resulting reduction in the number of developing rhombencephalon neurons.
